argument_summary: The rejection is supportable on the existing admissible record, but only on a bounded theory: the file shows a material unresolved risk at approval time, not a proven control failure. BPROC-033-D shows an unresolved storage-control inconsistency, and BPROC-033-E says approval should not proceed until storage controls are clarified if they remain unresolved. That core unresolved diligence issue is reinforced, though not independently dispositive, by BPROC-033-C (informal, undocumented quality process) and BPROC-033-B (one late quality artifact in prior work). BPROC-033-A cuts the other way on price, but lower cost does not cure unresolved control diligence. On that record, rejection is defensible as a risk-based procurement decision without needing to reopen the vendor review.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not require proof of a reject-level control failure if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk. It also expressly distinguishes questionnaire inconsistencies and quality-process gaps from a proven failure. The compliant framing is therefore narrow: rejection rests on unresolved risk that procurement said required follow-up before approval, with supporting process and execution concerns, not on any claim that the vendor failed a logged control test.
claims_about_business_cost: No reopening is needed to make the packet defensible. Recasting the basis of the decision more precisely avoids avoidable churn and preserves procurement velocity while staying within the policy standard for a risk-based rejection.
concessions: The admissible record does not show a formally logged failed control test.
Quality-process gaps and the questionnaire inconsistency are not, by themselves, proof of a reject-level control failure.
The case for rejection is moderate rather than strong and is strongest when stated as unresolved material risk at approval time.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No private or side-channel material is relied on in the public defense.
